Subset a GPU table with tibble's [ semantics

Source: R/generics.R
sub-.tbl_gpu.Rd

x[i, j] on a tbl_gpu follows tibble's [ rules, and for a grouped table dplyr's rules for a grouped data frame:

  • x[j] selects columns; x[i, j], x[i, ], x[, j], x[] are the 2-d forms. j is resolved first (names, positions, negative, logical) with tibble's vctrs_error_subscript_* errors, messages and calls.

  • Rows (i): positive positions gather in the given order (duplicates kept; out-of-range or NA gives an all-NA row), 0 is dropped, negative positions drop rows (out-of-range ones are ignored), a logical recycles from length 1 or must have length nrow (NA gives an NA row), a character is read as a row position (no row names).

  • drop = TRUE with exactly one result column returns that column as a vector (the only shape that executes a lazy table); with several columns it is ignored, except that a grouped table comes back ungrouped. In the 1-d form drop= warns and is ignored (a grouped table is still ungrouped, as in dplyr).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
x[i, j, drop = FALSE]

Arguments

x

A tbl_gpu object.

i

Row subscript (or, in the 1-d form, the column subscript).

j

Column subscript.

drop

If TRUE and the result has one column, return the column.

Value

A tbl_gpu, or a vector when drop = TRUE selects one column.

Details

Row selection runs on the GPU as one gather, and is added to the plan of a lazy table like any verb; column selection works as select.tbl_gpu() does. The result keeps the group variables that survive, and the table's .drop setting.

Row subscripts are validated against the real row count at call time whenever that is known without executing anything (an eager table, or a lazy one with no pending operations). On a lazy table with pending operations the row subscript is resolved when the plan runs, so its errors (same class, message and [ call) surface at collect()/compute().

A zero-column result (x[, 0], x[character()], x[, FALSE]) is an ungrouped zero-column table that keeps the row count (a lazy table with pending operations is computed first).

Divergences from tibble, all loud errors: duplicated columns (x[, c("a", "a")]) because a tbl_gpu cannot represent them, and matrix subscripts (x[m], and the soft-deprecated one-column matrix row subscript x[m, ], which tibble still accepts with a deprecation notice).
